hints: A later value no larger than an earlier value makes that earlier value useless while both are in the window.
Keep candidate values and their indices in increasing order in a deque.
Remove expired indices from the front and dominated values from the back.
analogy: The deque is a queue of minimum candidates; a cheaper, newer candidate retires older more expensive ones.
example: For [3,1,2] and k=2, both window minima are 1, and their XOR is 0.
algorithm: Generate values in order. Before inserting each value, discard expired indices from the front and values at least as large from the back; append the new value and index. Once the window is full, XOR the front value into the answer. Use wide arithmetic for the generator.
correctness: A removed back value can never be the minimum while the newer no-larger value remains, and the newer value expires later. The front is therefore the smallest unexpired candidate.
complexity: For n generated elements and window size k, O(n) time and O(k) space; each item enters and leaves the deque once.
